newsitem.title: USA: Mass Treasurer wants pension for "Big Dig" - paper.
newsitem.headline: Mass Treasurer wants pension for "Big Dig" - paper.

text.p: Massachusetts State Treasurer Joseph Malone offerd to pay the state's share of the $7.78 billion "Big Dig" highway project for Boston out of state pension funds, the Boston Globe said on Tuesday.
Malone, who is expected to be a Republican candidate for governor in 1998, proposed giving $2 billion of state funds to the Central Artery project over the next six years.

The paper said Gov William Weld wants to use the money to reduce the pension's unfunded liability, but the treasurer said the funds have done so well in the stock market that they no longer need it. Since Malone took over in 1991, the state pension funds have grown 12.2 percent a year, and unfunded liabilities have fallen to $6 billion from $13 billion.

Malone said his plan would free up $160 million a year in state debt that is earmarked for the Big Dig. This would let the state reduce its debt or pay for other projects, and also means Massachusetts no longer would have to borrow as much as $1.6 billion of federal funds, the Globe said.
The governor wants to speed up funding for the pension, to eliminate the unfunded liablity by 2019, but Malone's plan would stick to the presnet schedule, ending the liability by 2029.
The payments now consume five percent of state spending, about $1 billion a year, the paper added.
